active_inquiry.handoff_conclusion: Observed: M1 measured active +/-170 degree joint limits, collision-free sampled IK branches, and strong bounded actuation with rapid settling. M2 measured T1 at 68.0%, with 56 of 64 failures never reaching tolerance, exposing inadequate 14-20 cm training coverage for official inner radii. T2 fresh full-radius training measured 35.0% with 120/200 never-reached episodes, so coverage changes without preserving the outer controller were not viable in that tested recipe. Weighted transfer T3 measured 89.5%, with all 15 never-reached failures at radii 6.6-11.9 cm. T4 increased inner-radius exposure to 50% and measured 95.5%; only one episode never reached tolerance, while 20 episodes had hold interruptions. M5 artifact inspection further showed that 8 of its 9 failed episodes had nonzero interruptions, but 12 of the 20 interrupted episodes still succeeded and one failed episode had zero interruptions. Therefore staged transfer plus targeted inner-radius exposure is supported as an acquisition route, and hold robustness is a credible development bottleneck, but interruption counts are associated with most failures rather than established as their sole cause. The remaining competing explanations are sampled-data stabilization failure, hidden hold-history effects, or branch/geometry-specific representation limits. Claims remain limited to the measured candidates, panels, and recorded sampled evaluation semantics; branch identity, continuous internal-step behavior, and hold-history effects remain unmeasured.

request.description: Train PPO with the official full target-radius range while keeping the baseline observation, reward, and optimizer unchanged.
request.rationale: M2 measured 68% development success, with 56 of 64 failures never entering tolerance. request.description: Evaluate the late T2 checkpoint T2:checkpoint-120832 on a fresh 200-episode research panel.
request.rationale: T2 changed only the training radius range to the official 6-20 cm interval, but its training success remained zero and its terminal reward was far below T1. If development success is materially above zero, the route may need staged or curriculum coverage; if it is near zero, revert the direct coverage change and redesign the acquisition representation or learning schedule rather than iterate blindly.

request.description: Continue the competent T4 policy with the same 50% inner-radius and 50% outer-radius target curriculum, but forfeit accumulated hold-progress reward when an episode exits tolerance.
request.rationale: The unresolved distinction in I1 is whether the residual T4 failure tail is reducible sampled-data hold instability or instead reflects a branch or geometry-specific representation limit. M5 measured only one never-reached failure but nine total failures, eight with nonzero interruptions; it also showed long interruption runs after rapid first reach, including failures at inner and outer radii. The current reward gives zero forfeiture when a hold is interrupted, so it does not directly distinguish repeated tolerance entry from uninterrupted completion. This transfer keeps T4's demonstrated acquisition coverage and checkpoint while changing only the hold-exit consequence to the full accumulated hold-progress capital. If a follow-on candidate improves to at least 196/200 on a comparable research panel while preserving inner-radius success and reducing failure-linked interruptions, the hold-focused route is supported. If performance stagnates or failures remain concentrated by geometry despite the preserved curriculum, the result redirects the inquiry toward branch-aware representation or sampled-data stabilization rather than further hold-reward continuation.
